claim: Conjecture 1's `Prop` quantifies over `ProbDist S` at an infinite carrier, but the paper's Definition 36 defines a probability distribution only 'given a finite set S'; over an infinite `S` the rendering silently admits merely finitely-additive distributions (no countable additivity, no σ-algebra) that the paper never contemplated, so the Lean `Prop` is one particular sharpening of a one-sentence informal conjecture rather than 'nothing else changes'.
evidence: Paper §7.2: 'Theorem 3 can be generalized to finite-dimensional factored sets' (no formal statement). Paper Definition 36: 'Given a **finite** set $S$, a probability distribution on $S$ is a function $P:\mathcal{P}(S)\to\mathbb{R}$ …' with only finite additivity. Conjecture.lean:16-19 says the weakening is `[Finite S] → [Finite F.B]` and 'Nothing else changes', but dropping `Finite S` also changes *what `ProbDist S` ranges over*: e.g. on `ℕ × Bool` a density-style finitely-additive `P` with `P {s} = 0` for all `s` satisfies Definition 36 and Definition 37 vacuously, and such objects strengthen the `→` direction and weaken the `←` direction of the biconditional. Consequence a future agent must not miss: proving or refuting the Lean `Prop` would not by itself settle the paper's conjecture. No disclosure entry records this particular extension (dd:conjecture records the finiteness weakening; dd:probability records only that Definition 36 typechecks over any `S`).

claim: Proposition 24 (`orthogonal_iff_orthogonalGiven_top`) carries `[Finite F.B]`, which its statement does not need; the same is true of the supporting `orthogonalSub_ofSetoid` (L87) and `beforeSub_ofSetoid` (L93).
evidence: `historySub (ofSetoid X) = history X` is definitional under `generatesSub_ofSetoid` (both sides are `⋂₀` over the *same* family `{C | C ⊆ F.B ∧ …}`), so no finiteness is needed to identify Definition 24 with Definition 17 on partitions of `S`; and Proposition 24's two cases (`classes_top` for `Nonempty S`, vacuity plus `history X = ∅` for empty `S`) use nothing else. The unnecessary hypothesis is inherited from bundling Proposition 22's two sentences into one `[Finite F.B]` endpoint (`historySub_isLeast_and_eq_history`, SubpartitionHistory.lean:118), whose *first* conjunct genuinely needs finiteness. This contradicts the register sentences `dd:finiteness-minimal` — "finiteness hypotheses are carried only where they are used, never globally" (FiniteFactoredSets.lean:59) — and SubpartitionHistory.lean:11, "`[Finite F.B]` (finite dimension) is carried exactly where the paper's proofs use it". import FiniteFactoredSets.ConditionalOrthogonality
open FiniteFactoredSets FiniteFactoredSets.Subpartition
universe u
variable {S : Type u}
private lemma hsub (F : FactoredSet S) (X : Setoid S) :
    F.historySub (ofSetoid X) = F.history X := by
  simp only [FactoredSet.historySub, FactoredSet.history, FactoredSet.generatesSub_ofSetoid]
-- Proposition 24 with NO `[Finite F.B]`:
example (F : FactoredSet S) (X Y : Setoid S) :
    F.Orthogonal X Y ↔ F.OrthogonalGiven X Y ⊤ := by
  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty S with hS | hS
  · constructor
    · intro _ z hz
      obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := hz
      exact (IsEmpty.false y).elim
    · intro _
      rw [FactoredSet.orthogonal_def]
      have h : F.history X = ∅ := by
        have : (∅ : Set (Setoid S)) ∈ {C : Set (Setoid S) | C ⊆ F.B ∧ F.Generates C X} := by
          refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
          intro x hx
          obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := hx
          exact (IsEmpty.false y).elim
        have := Set.sInter_subset_of_mem this
        exact Set.subset_empty_iff.mp (by simpa [FactoredSet.history] using this)
      simp [h]
  · rw [FactoredSet.orthogonalGiven_def, FiniteFactoredSets.classes_top hS]
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, FactoredSet.orthogonalGivenSet_def,
      Subpartition.restrict_univ, hsub, FactoredSet.orthogonal_def]

claim: The recorded justification for `dd:subpartition` — "Mathlib has no partial-equivalence-relation structure to reuse, so this one is repo-generic" — is false against the pinned Mathlib (v4.31.0), which ships `Mathlib/Order/Partition/Basic.lean`: `Partition (E : Set α)` whose own module docstring says it "is equivalent to a transitive and symmetric binary relation `r : α → α → Prop` where `s` is the set of all `x` for which `r x x`", together with `Partition.Rel`, `Partition.partOf`, the same refinement `PartialOrder` (`Partition.rel_le_iff_le`), `Partition.instSemilatticeInf`, and `Partition.rel_rfl_iff` (dom = self-related points). This is equivalent to a transitive and symmetric binary relation `r : α → α → Prop` where `s` is the set of all `x` for which `r x x`"), :328 `def Rel`, :331 `rel_le_iff_le`, :349 `rel_rfl_iff`, :382 `def partOf`, :384 `partOf_subset`, :244 `instSemilatticeInf`, :361 `Rel.symm`, :365 `Rel.trans`, :367 `Rel.left_mem`. Lean side: `Subpartition.dom` (L66), `mem_dom_of_rel`/`mem_dom_of_rel'` (L68,L71), `part` (L75), `part_subset_dom` (L84), `part_eq_of_rel` (L87), `le_def` (L187), `instSemilatticeInf` (L204) each restate one of those on `Subpartition`. import Mathlib.Order.Partition.Basic
section
variable {α : Type} (E : Set α)
example (P : Partition E) (a b c : α) (h₁ : P.Rel a b) (h₂ : P.Rel b c) : P.Rel a c := h₁.trans h₂
example (P : Partition E) (a b : α) (h : P.Rel a b) : P.Rel b a := h.symm
example (P : Partition E) (a : α) : Set α := P.partOf a
example (P Q : Partition E) : P.Rel ≤ Q.Rel ↔ P ≤ Q := Partition.rel_le_iff_le
example (P Q : Partition E) : Partition E := P ⊓ Q
example (P : Partition E) (a : α) : P.Rel a a ↔ a ∈ E := Partition.rel_rfl_iff
end  -- compiles against this repo's toolchain (verified with `lake env lean`)
